plans.note: No liability/limitation heading appears in the outline; the numbering gaps (3, 4, 6, 9, 11) suggest unlisted sections, so scan text around the indemnity in sec-12 before concluding the cap is missing.

Section 12 is the indemnity; check whether TrueLink indemnifies Client for third-party IP and hosting misconduct or whether the flow is one-way from Client (sec-8 covenants may feed a Client-side indemnity).
Presence check: Client covenants in sec-8 and licence conditions in sec-2 are the only plausible homes for a restriction on Client's business lines; flag only if an actual restraint appears.
Look for sole-source or exclusive-hosting language in the licence grant (sec-2) or Client covenants (sec-8); hosting deals often bury exclusivity in the compensation terms.
Direction check on pricing terms in sec-5: MFN running to Client is fine; only a Client-side best-terms obligation would be a deviation.
Non-solicits commonly ride alongside confidentiality (sec-10) or Client covenants (sec-8); confirm scope, term and advertising carve-out if present.

No term/termination heading is listed; the unlisted sections (3, 4, 6, 9, 11) likely carry it — verify before reporting missing, and check sec-2 for licence revocation acting as de facto vendor termination.
Term/renewal mechanics are not in the supplied outline; if an unlisted term section exists, check auto-renewal length, notice window and any price uplift in sec-5.
Boilerplate governing law/venue sits in unlisted trailing sections; confirm the forum is NY, DE, CA or England and Wales and that disputes go to courts rather than foreign arbitration.
No assignment heading supplied; check general provisions and any licence transfer restriction in sec-2 that would block assignment to affiliates or a successor.

Direction check: confirm sec-2 and the sec-1 definitions leave Client owning its content, customer data and site materials, with no assignment or licence-back of Client IP to TrueLink; sec-10 may govern data as confidential information.
Core grant is sec-2 read with the sec-1 definitions (including Hosting Services); test scope for affiliates/contractors and whether the grant is revocable at will or otherwise conditioned.
Usage or records audits, if any, would sit in Client covenants (sec-8) or the compensation/reporting terms (sec-5); check notice, frequency and cost allocation.
Direction check: look in sec-5 for late fees or stipulated damages payable by Client, and in sec-7 for per-message penalties tied to the unsolicited e-mail covenant.
Section 8 covers Client warranties only; a TrueLink performance/hosting warranty would sit in an unlisted section (9 or 11) — confirm existence, duration and remedy before marking missing.
No insurance heading appears; given TrueLink hosts Client data, check near the indemnity (sec-12) for any insurance undertaking, otherwise treat as missing.
Compensation section is the likely home for minimum fees, guaranteed volumes or take-or-pay; if present, check for an exit or true-up.
No termination/transition heading supplied; check unlisted sections and the confidentiality return-of-materials language in sec-10, which may be the only data-return hook.
